draft.title: Current and non-current items
card: an asset that will be used or turned into cash within 12 months, or a liability that will be paid within 12 months. Cash, accounts receivable and inventory are current assets.
an asset the business will keep for longer than 12 months, or a liability it will not need to pay for more than 12 months. Equipment and vehicles are non-current assets.
Sort an item by when it will be used, received or paid, not by what it is. A bank loan repaid over five years is non-current, but the part due within 12 months is current.
The 12 months are counted forward from the date of the report. Accountants list current items separately from non-current items so the owner can see what is due soon.
draft.remember: Current means within 12 months. Non-current means longer than 12 months.

a.q: Which item would a service business record as a non-current asset?
opts: A delivery van it expects to use for six years
Cash held in its bank account
Money a client must pay in 30 days
Office stationery it will use up within months
a.why: The van will be used for much longer than 12 months, so it is non-current. Money owed by a client in 30 days is tempting because it is an asset, but it will be received within 12 months, so it is current.
a.clue: Which asset will the business still be using after 12 months?

b.q: Priya's Cleaning took a $60 000 bank loan to be repaid in equal yearly amounts over five years. How should the loan be shown at the start of the first year?
opts: Mostly non-current, with the next year's repayment current
All current, because the bank can ask for repayment
All non-current, because the loan lasts five years
All current, because it was borrowed this year
b.why: The part due within 12 months is a current liability, and the rest is due later, so it is non-current. Calling it all non-current is tempting because the loan lasts five years, but the next year's repayment must be paid within 12 months.
b.clue: Ask how much of the loan must be paid in the next 12 months.

a.best: A delivery van it expects to use for six years

b.best: Mostly non-current, with the next year's repayment current
